text: Channels, right? And what you can see here is that they overlap, but mildly, right? They overlap just a little bit. So this means that these signals that are sent in parallel will not interfere much because they do not overlap very much, right? So by transmitting in this way, you can send in parallel many electromagnetic signals at the same time. So this means that you can be fast because you are not sending just one signal at a time, but many in parallel. And even if you send many signals in parallel, they will not interfere too much because they are quite separated one from the other. So the overall data rate that you will be able to achieve depends on how many bits you send through each of these signals, right? So OFDM, orthogonal frequency division means that indeed you are sending in parallel multiple signals that are divided in frequency because they use different frequency subchannels.
